dataset_context_from_paper: De-identified individual-level data underlying the analyses reported in this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and subject to approval by the Makerere University School of Medicine Research Ethics Committee, due to participant privacy and consent restrictions. The dataset includes cognitive assessment scores (MMSE - Mini-Mental State Examination) and MRI measurements of medial temporal atrophy (MTA) and global cortical atrophy (GCA) used to evaluate diagnostic accuracy and comparative classification performance in dementia assessment.

dataset_identifier: Shen et al. supplementary GWAS data
dataset_context_from_paper: Publicly available datasets were analyzed in this study. The dataset used corresponds to supplementary GWAS data published by Shen et al. and is available at the provided URL. Genome-wide association summary statistics were processed and integrated across 26 analytically distinct population cohorts. SNP identifiers were standardized using rsIDs, and overlap across datasets was evaluated using scripted, reproducible workflows. All SNPs identified across the included studies were compiled into a structured database with unique cohort identifiers to prevent double-counting of genetic signals derived from overlapping samples.

dataset_identifier: Arizona Study of Aging and Neurodegenerative Disorders
dataset_context_from_paper: A 29-year longitudinal study providing autopsy subjects for synuclein pathology analysis. The study included 178 autopsied subjects: 50 neuropathologically confirmed Parkinson's disease (PD) subjects, 34 incidental Lewy body disease (ILBD) subjects, and 94 non-demented controls without clinical parkinsonism or CNS synuclein pathology (NLB subjects). Comprehensive survey of gastrointestinal (GI) tract synuclein pathology was conducted across 1,780 GI sites using synuclein seeding amplification assays (SAA) and phosphorylated synuclein (pSyn) immunohistochemistry (IHC). Results showed PD subjects had highest proportion of positive subjects (96%) and GI sites (90%), followed by ILBD subjects (71% subjects, 37% sites) and NLB subjects (11% subjects, 2% sites).

Participants were part of the BIOCARD study including 136 cognitively normal individuals and 21 participants with mild cognitive impairment (mean age = 71.7 years). The study investigated cross-sectional relationships between actigraphy-estimated total volume of physical activity (TVPA) and sleep patterns [total sleep time (TST), sleep efficiency (SE)] with cognitive performance (n = 157). In a subset of participants (n = 135), physical activity and sleep measures were evaluated in relationship to resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) measures of large-scale network connectivity, and positron emission tomography (PET) measures of amyloid-ß. Linear regression analyses assessed associations between TVPA, TST, and SE with cognition, connectivity within default-mode, salience, and fronto-parietal control networks, and network modularity.

Datasets can be requested through formal research applications to the Washington Heights-Inwood Columbia Aging Project. Requests to access these datasets should be directed to the Columbia University Alzheimer's Disease Research Center.

Datasets can be requested through formal research applications to the Genetic Studies of Alzheimer's Disease in Caribbean Hispanics (EFIGA). Requests to access these datasets should be directed to the Columbia University Alzheimer's Disease Research Center.
Data may also be requested from the Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention and the Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center via the provided portal.

Data collection and sharing for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) were funded by the National Institute on Aging (National Institutes of Health Grant U19AG024904). The study evaluated P-tau217 and APOE-ε4 biomarkers in longitudinal analyses with time-dependent AUC values exceeding 0.75 at most time points.

Research reported for HABS-HD was supported by the NIA/NIH under Award Numbers R01AG054073, R01AG058533, R01AG070862, P41EB015922 and U19AG078109. Data was used in cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses evaluating P-tau217 and APOE-ε4 prognostic performance.

Data may be requested from the Religious Orders Study and Memory and Aging Project (ROSMAP). The dataset was used in pooled longitudinal analyses with stratification applied for covariates that violated the proportional hazards assumption.

We collected data from 922 participants in the Bio‐Hermes‐001 multi‐site study (age mean±SD = 72±6.6; 57% female; years of education mean±SD = 15±2.71; primary language English), classified as cognitively unimpaired (n = 402), mild cognitively impaired (n = 298), or probable Alzheimer's dementia (n = 242) based on clinical consensus and neuropsychological evaluation. We split participants, each including 2000 speech and drawing DCR metrics and age, into training (80%) and test (20%) sets, ensuring equal rates of functional impairment across sets (Functional Activities Questionnaire ≥ 6; 25% rate). We performed recursive feature elimination on 10‐fold cross‐validated random forests (5 repetitions) on the training set to identify the best model and feature set. Model performance was evaluated on the test set.

930 participants (mean age 72.0±6.7; 56.8% female; 23% minorities) in the Bio-Hermes-001 study were classified as cognitively unimpaired, mild cognitive impairment, or probable Alzheimer's dementia, and 35.1% were Aβ+ on 18F-florbetapir PET scan. Participants underwent digital cognitive assessment using the Linus Health Digital Clock and Recall (DCR), which captured drawing metrics, speech and acoustic features, and temporal-spatial features of stylus manipulation. Blood-based biomarkers were measured including Lilly pTau-217, Quanterix pTau-181, and C2N Aβ42/40. The DCR-based algorithm (LinusAD) used age, APOE status, and these digital and biomarker features to predict cognitive impairment status and brain amyloid-beta status on 18F-florbetapir PET imaging.
Raw and normalized count matrices of single-cell RNA sequencing and CRISPR interference screen datasets from the dCas9-KRAB line. These data are available at GEO under accession code GSE306200.
Raw and normalized count matrices of single-cell RNA sequencing and CRISPR interference screen datasets from the dCas9-KRAB line. These data are available at GEO under accession code GSE306202.

The dCas9-KRAB iPSC line was developed at the Allen Institute for Cell Science and available through the Coriell Institute for Medical Research (AICS-0090). This line was derived from the WTC parental line released by the Conklin Laboratory at the J. David Gladstone Institute. The AICS-0090 dCas9-KRAB iPSC line has been validated for genomic integrity, pluripotency, and differentiation into multiple lineages.
The BR09 and BR28 iPSC lines were generated from white blood cells collected from participants in the Rush Memory and Aging Project (MAP) by the New York Stem Cell Foundation.

Physiological data were processed using a custom pipeline scripted in AcqKnowledge software (v4.4). Four C9+ participants were tested but excluded from this study due to invalid physiological data (one participant had a sensor fail during testing, and three participants had cardiac arrhythmias for more than 10 percent of the baseline period). The study measured baseline RSA (respiratory sinus arrhythmia) in C9orf72 pathogenic expansion carriers to assess parasympathetic function and its relationship to disease progression in frontotemporal dementia.

The data from the DIAN study can be requested online at https://dian.wustl.edu/. The study includes cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers from mutation carriers and non-carriers, including measurements of Amyloid beta (Aβ), phosphorylated Tau (pTau), total Tau (tTau), SNAP-25, Neurogranin (Ng), Neurofilament Light (NfL), visinin-like protein 1 (VILIP-1), YKL40, and soluble TREM2 (sTREM2). The dataset includes clinical dementia rating scale (CDR) scores and estimated years to symptom onset (EYO) for mutation carriers. CSF biomarker measurements were available for varying sample sizes: SNAP (n=330), Ng (n=331), VILIP1 (n=330), YKL40 (n=331), NfL (n=165), sTREM2 (n=164). The study examined biomarker trajectories and their relationships to grey matter network values across different disease stages and mutation types (PSEN1, PSEN2, and APP).

BioFINDER-2 cohort used for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarker analysis. Study examined CSF methods including immunoassay and mass spectrometry approaches. Biomarkers measured included amyloid β (Aβ) and phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217). All study participants provided written informed consent, and local institutional review boards approved the studies. The study followed the Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy (STARD) reporting guideline.

The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) was used as one of the cohorts in this multi-cohort study examining sex-specific differences in Alzheimer's disease biomarkers and cognitive outcomes. Demographic and clinical variables including cognition, metabolic, and lifestyle factors were extracted and underwent quality control to ensure direct translation across cohorts.

data_repository: Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease trial and the companion Longitudinal Evaluation of Amyloid Risk and Neurodegeneration
dataset_context_from_paper: The Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease trial (A4/Learn) was included as one of the cohorts in this multi-cohort analysis. Demographic variables, cognition measures, metabolic and lifestyle factors were extracted and quality controlled for consistency across cohorts in the sex-specific analysis of Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.

The Harvard Aging Brain Study (HABS) was utilized as one of the cohorts in this multi-cohort study. Demographic and clinical variables including cognition, metabolic, and lifestyle factors were extracted and underwent quality control procedures to ensure consistency across the different cohorts used in the sex-specific analysis.

We studied 706 primarily English-speaking participants from Bio-Hermes-001 study (age mean±SD = 71.5±6.7; 58.9% female; years of education mean±SD = 15.4±2.7; 85.1% White; 9.3% Hispanic), classified a priori as cognitively unimpaired (CU; n = 360), mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 234), or probable Alzheimer's dementia (pAD; n = 111) based on expert consensus and neuropsychological evaluation. Bias was compared by bootstrapping two multiple linear regressions predicting either Z-scaled DCR or MMSE scores using race, ethnicity, sex, education, and age as predictors.

We also studied 770 participants in a prescreening study for AD-related clinical trials (age mean±SD = 68.8±13.2; 64% female; education = 15±2.6; 78% White; 20% Hispanic) including CU (n = 338), MCI (n = 178), and pAD (N = 254). For each dataset, bias was compared by bootstrapping two multiple linear regressions predicting either Z-scaled DCR or MMSE scores using race, ethnicity, sex, education, and age as predictors.

Participants were enrolled in ARTFL LEFFTDS Longitudinal Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration consortium (ALLFTD) – a multisite study that includes participants from the Advancing Research and Treatment for Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration (ARTFL) and Longitudinal Evaluation of Familial Frontotemporal Dementia Subjects (LEFFTDS) studies. Each participant underwent extensive clinical interviews and examinations, structural MRI, and blood biomarker sampling. Participants with a primary clinical diagnosis of bvFTD who met formal criteria for probable bvFTD at one or more study visits were included in the analyses. In the study population, genetic status was known in 78% of participants with 49% having sporadic bvFTD, 14% having a C9orf72 mutation, 6% having a GRN mutation, 9% having a MAPT mutation, and 22% having unknown genetic status. Disease severity was defined based on Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR® ) plus NACC FTLD Behavior & Language Domains global score.

Raw sequencing data of brain tissue have been deposited in the Sequence Read Archive under project no. PRJNA1265217. Raw transcriptomes from 4 sequencing lanes were mapped using the nf-core RNA-Seq module. Gene-level counts were extracted from the mapped data and used as input for differentially expressed gene (DEG) analysis.

PPMI data can be accessed by permission from the Parkinson's Progression Marker Initiative. PPMI whole transcriptomes and genomes were collected, sampled, sequenced, and genotyped as previously described. Transcriptomes, genomes, demographic information, signs and symptoms, assay results, and cognitive information were downloaded from LONI Image and Data Archive (LIDA, downloaded April-August 2024). For larger datasets, from the PPMI whole blood sample groups, variance-stabilized transformation normalization was applied using DESeq2. Metadata files were generated with the factor group combined, which categorized samples into 3 groups: PD HPgV+, PD HPgV–, and CT.
For small-sample RADC brain tissue dataset, DEG was performed using the Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric test to account for small group sizes and nonnormal data distribution.

Human donor samples from the University of Washington were provided from the following studies: Adult Changes in Thought (ACT) (5U19 AG066567). Snap-frozen cerebellar and hippocampal tissue was homogenized using N-PER Neuronal Protein Extraction Reagent to produce protein lysates used in this study.

The dataset was used for connectomic analysis to investigate network measures and validate that motion did not introduce artifactual differences.

The BIOCARD Study dataset was used for connectomic analysis. Similar results to the low- and high-motion dataset comparison were found for connectomics in the BIOCARD dataset, with no statistically significant differences in the 5 investigated network measures, confirming no artifactual differences were introduced by motion.

Omics data for BRCA dataset were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA) through Broad GDAC Firehose. PAM50 breast cancer subtypes of BRCA dataset were obtained from TCGA biolinks. For BRCA recurrence prediction, SYCP3 and HPSE2 emerged as stable mRNA biomarkers appearing across both gradient and core sets; somatic alterations in CDS2 and AMY2B were prioritized in the SNV modality.
Omics data for LGG, and the grade information for LGG dataset were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA) through Broad GDAC Firehose.
Cancer prognosis omic data PRAD were obtained from Xena TCGA Pan-Cancer web with their corresponding clinical data from TCGA. For PRAD, the most stable SNV drivers included SRGAP3.

dataset_identifier: Study dataset - 186 MDD patients and 67 healthy controls
data_repository: Supplementary information files (available at MP's website)
dataset_context_from_paper: Gene expression study quantifying mRNA expression in PBMCs of 186 individuals with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and 67 healthy controls (HCs). Authors measured expression of key genes from three physiological domains: ER stress (XBP1u, XBP1s, ATF4), inflammasome activation (NLRC4, NLRP3, ASC), and mitochondrial biogenesis (DNM1L, MFN2). TaqMan Gene Expression Assay primers were used for quantification. All samples were run blind to diagnosis in triplicate. Mean CT values for reference gene GAPDH were 23.68 ± 0.93 for HC group and 24.19 ± 0.98 for MDD group.

The study included 192 participants without dementia (14 with mild cognitive impairment [MCI]) from the BIOCARD Study (mean age = 68), of whom 52 (27%) were Aβ positive (measured via PET). Multiple linear regression analyses tested whether hippocampal mean diffusivity (MD), a DWI‐derived metric, moderated the associations between tau accumulation on PET (within subregions defined as Braak stage I‐V) and global and domain‐specific cognitive composite scores (episodic memory, executive function, visuospatial abilities, and language), while controlling for age, sex, education, APOE genetic risk, amyloid positivity status, and hippocampal volume.

The MCSA study makes de-identified data available to qualified researchers upon reasonable request. The dataset was analyzed using hypergraph analysis to examine disease trajectories, considering CCC, DCC, and ESCC as source conditions and MCI as the target condition. The analysis examined sequence and participant coverage to highlight dominant patterns in chronic condition progression.

The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) is referenced as one of multiple longitudinal cohort studies used in this research on neuroimaging and cognitive decline. The study involves analysis of tract-specific white matter measurements and their association with cognitive status.
The Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) is included as one of the longitudinal cohort studies contributing to the analysis of white matter tracts and cognitive outcomes in aging populations.

data_repository: Biomarkers of Cognitive Decline Among Normal Adults
dataset_context_from_paper: The Biomarkers of Cognitive Decline Among Normal Adults (BIOCARD) study is referenced as a source for examining cognitive decline and associated biomarkers in cognitively unimpaired individuals.
The Rush Memory and Aging Project (MAP) is included among the cohort studies used for tract-specific white matter analysis and cognitive outcomes assessment.
The Minority Aging Research Study (MARS) is referenced as a contributing cohort study for examining cognitive and neuroimaging outcomes in diverse aging populations.
The National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) is cited as a data resource for Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment research, providing standardized clinical and cognitive assessments.
The Religious Orders Study (ROS) is included as one of the longitudinal cohort studies contributing neuroimaging and cognitive data for white matter tract analysis.
The Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project (VMAP) is referenced as a source cohort for examining memory and aging-related changes in white matter tracts.

The Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention (WRAP) is included among the cohort studies used for analyzing white matter tract-specific measurements and their association with cognitive status in at-risk populations.

Independent dataset from the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP), comprised of WGS data from ∼30,000 individuals, was used to confirm increased CHIP mutations in AD versus control (p < 0.02, OR = 1.32). Analysis was driven by individuals with APOE ε3/ε3 genotype. CHIP mutations in AD patients showed stronger positive selection than in controls.

Molecular-barcoded deep gene panel sequencing (∼400X) was used to examine CHIP mutations in 298 blood samples from AD and neurotypical individuals 60 years and older. AD patients exhibited significantly higher burden of CHIP mutations compared to age-matched controls (p < 2e-7, odds ratio = 2.89), particularly in low-frequency variants often not captured by standard WGS. This increase was driven by individuals with APOE ε3/ε3 genotype and absent in ε4 carriers.

Baseline visit data from participants were obtained from three longitudinal aging studies conducted by Rush University through their Alzheimer's Disease Research Center: The Memory and Aging Project (MAP), African American Clinical Core (AA Core), and the Minority Adult Research Study (MARS). MAP began data collection in 1997 by recruiting older adults living in retirement communities throughout Chicago and northeastern Illinois with the goal of studying cognitive and motor declines in the context of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). All studies' inclusion criteria require annual clinical evaluations, blood draws, and neuropsychological testing. Participants from each study were given a battery consisting of 21 various cognitive performance tests in an annual evaluation. Of the tests, 19 were averaged and subset into domains to create a global composite score consisting of: Episodic Memory, Semantic Memory, Working Memory, Visuospatial ability, and Perceptual Speed. Depressive symptoms were measured using a 10-item short form version of the 20-item version of the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression (CES-D) scale.

The Memory and Aging Project (MAP) began data collection in 1997 by recruiting older adults living in retirement communities throughout Chicago and northeastern Illinois with the goal of studying cognitive and motor declines in the context of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). MAP recruits those without known dementia at baseline. Participants undergo annual clinical evaluations, blood draws, and neuropsychological testing including a battery of 21 cognitive performance tests.

Beginning in 2004, the Minority Adult Research Study (MARS) is primarily focused on cognitive decline and risk of AD in African American/Black cohorts in the Chicago area. MARS recruits those without known dementia at baseline. All studies' inclusion criteria require annual clinical evaluations, blood draws, and neuropsychological testing.

Beginning in 2008, the African American Clinical Core (AA Core) is primarily focused on cognitive decline and risk of AD in African American/Black cohorts in the Chicago area, with AA Core specializing on the transition from normal aging to early stages of dementia. AA Core includes those with and without dementia at their baseline visits. All studies' inclusion criteria require annual clinical evaluations, blood draws, and neuropsychological testing.

RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data are available at the NCBI GEO under the SuperSeries accession GSE206603. Normalized count matrices for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data are provided in Supplementary files. The data was used to characterize chromatin accessibility changes and gene expression changes across FAD mutations relative to NDC (normal donor controls). ATAC-seq peak accessibility changes were analyzed in promoter- and enhancer-located regions, and RNA-seq gene expression was measured across all FAD mutations. The dataset was used for differential accessibility analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, transcription factor binding site analysis using the cisBP database, and construction of regulatory interaction networks.

Code for all analysis is available for download from https://github.com/SubramaniamLab/FAD-Multiomics-Manuscript and 10.5281/zenodo.8267332. This includes analysis code for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data processing, differential accessibility analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, transcription factor activity analysis, and regulatory network construction.

Raw mass spectrometry files from CSF proteomic sequencing of ADNI participants. Baseline CSF samples were digested and labeled with TMTpro reagents, fractionated by high-pH reversed-phase chromatography, and analyzed by liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry. Raw files were searched using FragPipe v22.0 against UniProt human protein database with TMT-16 plex parameters. After quality control filtering (proteins measured in ≥200 subjects, removal of outlier samples >4 standard deviations from mean of first two principal components, batch effect correction), 2961 proteins in CSF proteomes were retained for downstream statistical analysis examining 10 candidate NPS brain causal proteins in relation to baseline and incident neuropsychiatric symptom domains.

Phenotypic and CSF proteomic data from participants recruited by the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative study (ADNI). Started in 2003, ADNI is a multicenter longitudinal study designed to track the progression of Alzheimer's disease across normal aging, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and AD dementia. CSF was collected at baseline and proteins were extracted for proteomic sequencing.

miRNA data and miR-QTL summary statistics presented in this paper can be found with Synapse ID syn51247298. The miRNA data were generated in this study and compared and integrated with multiple existing datasets and resources. miRNA sequencing reads were independently mapped to two reference miRNA databases: miRBase and MirGeneDB.

Transcriptomic data and eQTL and pQTL summary statistics used for host gene co-localization can be found with Synapse ID syn51150434. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiles from postmortem dlPFC samples were available from a published study. Transcriptomic data included 589 ROS/MAP participants (376 female and 213 male, mean age 89 years), sequenced using Illumina HiSeq and aligned to GRCh38. Low-abundance transcripts (<1 RPM for ≥50% of samples) were filtered, and normalized log2-transformed counts were adjusted for batch effects, RIN, PMI, age, and clinical diagnosis.

Whole-brain multi-band functional MRI data (duration = 10 min) collected at wakeful rest from sporadic EOAD (n = 239) and cognitively unimpaired (CU) (n = 68) participants from the LEADS cohort. Participants underwent preprocessing, confound removal, and quality control of MRI data. Residual functional timeseries data were used to calculate seed-based functional connectivity of each anatomically distinct cortical region within the EOAD signature. Seed-based connectivity maps were compared between EOAD and CU participants while controlling for age, sex, and estimates of in-scanner head motion. In EOAD patients, stronger functional connectivity within multiple networks was associated with worse cognitive impairment and greater atrophy in the EOAD signature.

dataset_identifier: Rush Alzheimer's Disease Centre resource sharing hub
dataset_context_from_paper: All data used in these analyses are available from the Rush Alzheimer's Disease Centre resource sharing hub. The dataset includes longitudinal kidney function measurements with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) calculated from serum creatinine measured yearly as part of a basic metabolic panel performed by Quest Diagnostics. eGFR was estimated using the CKD-EPI formula. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) was defined as eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73 m². The study examined factors supporting preserved kidney function during aging in the context of chronic kidney disease risk.

dataset_identifier: Ghana Births and Deaths Registry Mortality Register
dataset_context_from_paper: The two primary sources of annual mortality data are the BDR's administrative Mortality Register (MR) and the Population and Housing Census (PHC). Data used for the analysis is publicly available on the website of the Births and Death registry at https://bdr.gov.gh/downloads/. The dataset contains mortality records from Ghana's central birth and death registration system, which aims to provide vital statistics adequate and efficient for public health planning.

dataset_identifier: Ghana 2021 Population and Housing Census - Volume 3H Fertility and Mortality
dataset_context_from_paper: The two primary sources of annual mortality data are the BDR's administrative Mortality Register (MR) and the Population and Housing Census (PHC), conducted approximately every ten years by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) through surveys. Data used for the analysis is publicly available through the Ghana Statistical Service's (2021 PHC General Report Vol 3H Fertility and Mortality). This dataset provides mortality statistics and fertility data collected through national census surveys.

In silico text-mining strategy using the pubmed.mineR package of RStudio to systematically collect, organize and analyze relevant published findings from PubMed. By combining automated text mining with manual curation, researchers identified 2357 genes implicated in prostate cancer from published literature.

FDA approved drugs sourced from ZINC database. The most frequent hub gene was docked with FDA approved drugs sourced from ZINC database. Two promising drug candidates (Budesonide and ICG) were then subjected to molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate the stability of their complexes with Src.

The Src protein (PDB ID: 2H8H) was selected as the target for molecular docking with FDA-approved drugs. Src protein structure was used for molecular docking studies and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate drug-protein complex stability.

When applied to CNV derived from whole genome sequencing data of the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project, the proposed methods identify additional CNVs associated with Alzheimer's Disease (AD). These identified CNVs overlap with several known AD-risk genes and are significantly enriched by biological processes related to neuron structures and functions crucial in AD development.

Large public ASL dataset comprising subjects acquired using the pCASL-2D-EPI sequence. High-SNR CBF maps from QTAB were used as source datasets for training the distribution-remapping framework. Total of 750 subjects in QTAB and PTBP combined.

Large public ASL dataset comprising subjects acquired using the pCASL-2D-EPI sequence. High-SNR CBF maps from PTBP were used as source datasets for training the distribution-remapping framework. Total of 750 subjects in QTAB and PTBP combined.

Subset of the ADNI3 dataset acquired using PASL-2D-EPI sequence. Only 18 subjects were included from this dataset to simulate limited data condition for evaluating the proposed method's generalizability across different ASL sequences.

dataset_context_from_paper: Specialized PASL-3D-EPSI sequence used to acquire ASL data from 10 healthy volunteers on a 3T MR system (MAGNETOM Prisma, Siemens Healthineers, Erlangen, Germany). Local dataset partitioned into training and testing datasets as detailed in Table S1.

dataset_context_from_paper: pCASL-3D-GRASE sequence used to collect ASL data from 10 subjects. Local dataset partitioned into training and testing datasets as detailed in Table S1.

Using data from Data Freeze 15, participants were categorized as asymptomatic (CDR = 0), mildly symptomatic (CDR = 0.5) or having dementia (CDR > 0.5). Study compared biomarkers between 17 carriers of the A431E PSEN1 mutation and 31 carriers of the V717I APP mutation using linear models adjusting for estimated years to symptom onset. Fluid, MRI, PiB and FDG PET biomarkers were analyzed in carriers of these autosomal dominant Alzheimer's disease mutations at comparable clinical disease stages.

data_repository: Central Neuroimaging Data Archive (Informatics Core at Washington University)
dataset_context_from_paper: The Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) is a longitudinal study collecting biospecimens and data from autosomal dominant Alzheimer disease (ADAD) families. Data and biospecimens are maintained in a central repository at Washington University. Derived data and raw images are stored in the Central Neuroimaging Data Archive. The study includes standardized assessments across 14 sites: clinical assessment, psychometric testing, non-fasting blood collection for genetics, fasting CSF and blood collection, MRI, amyloid imaging with 11C-PIB-PET, and fluorodeoxyglucose-PET (FDG-PET). The study includes mutation carriers and non-carrier control group individuals from the same families, with synchronized assessment structure allowing cross-modality comparisons within 3-month visit windows. The longitudinal nature provides data on how AD biomarkers change over time in individual participants.

RNA from a total of 183 human postmortem brain samples were used to compare the Agilent 4200 TapeStation's RIN equivalent (RINe) and DV200 to the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer's RIN. The study evaluated RNA integrity measurements across these 183 parallel RNA samples, finding that RIN and RINe values only weakly correlate with an r² of 0.393 and an average difference of 3.2 RIN units.

The datasets generated during the current study are not publicly available due to the sensitive nature of this human subjects data set, but are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. Currently human data generated in this research is quality controlled and preserved with the DIAN Obs Biostatistics Core and in process to transition to the Washington University Becker Medical Library's Digital Commons Data Repository and the Research Infrastructure Service (RIS). The dataset includes clinical data, fluid biomarker samples, brain samples, genomic data, imaging data, and cognition data. As of December 2022, DIAN Obs has received 288 data requests and 114 tissue requests, with 231 and 85 requests fulfilled, respectively. Image data will be available to approved investigators in post-processed formats via the DIAN Central Neuroimaging Data Archive (CNDA) after a formal DUA has been signed.

Data sets from the WI ADRC and WRAP studies were analyzed in this research. These cohorts provided cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples and clinical data for proteomics analysis examining the relationship between CSF biomarkers and Alzheimer's disease pathology categories.

Microglia eQTL summary statistics may be requested through the European Genome-Phenome Archive (EGAD00001005736) and the Wellcome Sanger Institute Data Access Committee. These data provide expression quantitative trait loci information supporting the functional genomic analysis of genes near GWAS-identified SNPs.

The EMIF-AD proteomics data may be requested from the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository with the data set identifier PXD019910. This dataset contains mass spectrometry-based CSF proteomics data from 242 participants of European ancestry used for replication of CSF GPX3 levels across Alzheimer's disease pathology categories.

The Knight ADRC proteomic data are available at NIAGADS: NG00102 collection and can be interactively explored at http://ngi.pub:3838/ONTIME_Proteomics/. This includes discovery (n=1168) and replication (n=597) CSF proteomics datasets from Washington University in St. Louis measured using aptamer-based proteomics platform, examining GPX3 levels across Alzheimer's disease pathology categories.

The European Medical Information Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Multimodal Biomarker Discovery (EMIF-AD MBD) study (n=242) provided replication proteomics cohort data. MS-derived CSF GPX3 levels were analyzed by AT category, with no significant difference observed (P=0.96) even when stratified by rs34294852 genotypes or controlling for age, sex, or study site.

dataset_identifier: MAP, ADNI, DIAN, Pau, Ruiz studies
dataset_context_from_paper: Additional replication proteomics cohorts were used including the Memory and Aging Project (MAP) at Knight ADRC (n=948), Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI; n=758), Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN; n=495), Pau (n=232), and Ruiz (n=632) studies. These cohorts provided CSF proteomics data for validating GPX3 findings across multiple populations.

Mass spectrometry (MS) CSF proteomics data from the University of Wisconsin (mean age 66.1; 59.9% female; all of European ancestry) was used as the discovery dataset. Among genes closest to GWAS-identified SNPs rs871269 and rs34294852 (TNIP1 and GPX3), only GPX3 was identified and quantified in this discovery CSF dataset. ANOVA analyses examined the relationship of CSF GPX3 with CSF amyloid- and tau-defined categories of AD (total n=137; 56 A-T-, 39 A+T-, and 42 A+T+).

Sporadic FTLD cohort with neuropathology-confirmed FTLD-tau and FTLD-TDP, clinically diagnosed PSP-Richardson Syndrome, and controls. Participants (n = 95; mean age = 69 ± 6 yrs; 48% female). CSF TMEM106B and NfL protein levels were quantified with aptamer-based proteomics. Associations between biomarkers and disease severity measures including CDR®+NACC-FTLD were determined with linear regressions. Associations with brain volumes were determined within voxel-based morphometry framework.

Familial FTLD cohort comprised of presymptomatic and symptomatic FTLD mutation carriers with family non-carrier controls (n = 179; mean age = 49 ± 13 yrs; 53% female). CSF TMEM106B and NfL protein levels were quantified with aptamer-based proteomics. Associations between biomarkers and disease severity measures including CDR®+NACC-FTLD sum of boxes were determined with mixed linear models. Brain volume associations were determined with voxel-based morphometry. CSF TMEM106B concentrations were influenced by TMEM106B rs1990622 genotype.

The proteomics data of the EMIF-AD MDB cohort have been deposited to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository with the dataset identifiers PXD019910. Tandem mass spectrometry-based measurement of proteomics data and preprocessing, including quality control and normalization of the CSF proteomic data for EMIF-AD MBD were performed. Protein abundances were corrected for technical variation between 16-plex experiments using the internal reference scaling procedure or tandem mass tag (TMT) data. After batch correction, protein abundance values were log2-transformed and harmonized between cohorts. The dataset includes 57 proteins analyzed in relation to Alzheimer's disease pathophysiology and cognitive status (cognitively normal, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease), with additional assessment of depression symptoms using Geriatric Depression Scale scoring.

data_repository: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set
dataset_context_from_paper: The paper references NACC-UDS (National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center Uniform Data Set) in the abbreviations section, indicating its use in the study of frontotemporal dementia and related neurodegenerative conditions. This standardized dataset is commonly used for longitudinal evaluation and clinical characterization of dementia patients.

data_repository: Advancing Research and Treatment in Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration/Longitudinal Evaluation of Familial Frontotemporal Dementia Subjects
dataset_context_from_paper: The paper references ALLFTD (Advancing Research and Treatment in Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration/Longitudinal Evaluation of Familial Frontotemporal Dementia Subjects) as a key dataset resource. This longitudinal study evaluates familial frontotemporal dementia subjects and is supported by NIH grants U01AG045390, U54NS092089, and U01AG016976.

GLIOGENE consortium glioma GWAS summary statistics are available from the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) under accession number EGAS00001003372. These summary statistics were used for candidate gene prioritization through integration with multi-omics data in the study workflow.

FinnGen R9 glioma GWAS summary statistics are available from https://www.finngen.fi/en/access_results. These summary statistics were integrated with multi-omics data for candidate gene prioritization in the study.

The reference panel, which is the merged genotype data from UK10K and 1000 Genomes Project Phase 3, is available from the EGA under accession number EGAD00001000776. This reference panel was used to generate Summary QTL database reference panel weights for TWAS and PWAS analyses.

Summary QTL database reference panel weights generated for this study used in TWAS and PWAS are available at https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/_b_TWAS_PWAS_gene_expression_prediction_models_b_/28080035. These gene expression prediction models were used for transcriptome-wide and proteome-wide association studies.

PLAC-seq, snATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data were downloaded from https://github.com/nottalexi/brain-cell-type-peak-files. These epigenomic datasets were used for multi-omics integration and cell-type-specific analysis.
pcHi-C was downloaded from GSE113481. This 3D chromatin interaction dataset was used for annotating cis-regulatory elements and genomic interactions in the analysis of glioma susceptibility loci.
Bulk ATAC was downloaded from GSE113480. This chromatin accessibility dataset was used for epigenomic analysis and multi-omics integration in candidate gene prioritization.

In a recent study using the EMIF-AD cohort (N = 886) we examined associations between blood DNAm and 15 CSF biomarkers of AD and neurodegeneration. The study identified five Bonferroni-significant differentially methylated positions (DMPs) in the CHI3L1 gene (encoding YKL-40) associated with CSF YKL-40, a biomarker of glial activation and neuroinflammation. The stringent QC pipeline resulted in 882 high-quality samples (662 with NfL measurements) and 861,666 CpG probes retained for analysis. DNAm data processing used the watermelon package implementing stringent quality control, excluding samples and probes based on detection P values and bead counts, followed by quantile normalization.

Publicly available human data from TBI used in this study. Samples associated with psychiatric diseases or drug abuse were excluded. Only samples with an RNA integrity number (RIN) ≥ 6 were retained for analysis. The study utilized this dataset along with GTEx for developing a brain-specific transcriptomic clock.

Publicly available human data from GTEx accessed for bulk tissue expression. GTEx metadata with age details can be accessed upon request. Samples associated with psychiatric diseases or drug abuse were excluded. Only samples with an RNA integrity number (RIN) ≥ 6 were retained for analysis. Used as a primary data source for training the brain-specific transcriptomic clock.

Data from the RNAseq Harmonization Study available upon request at AD Knowledge Portal. Samples associated with psychiatric diseases or drug abuse were excluded. Only samples with an RNA integrity number (RIN) ≥ 6 were retained for analysis. Data collection was supported through Cure PSP, Mayo and Michael J Fox foundations, Arizona Department of Health Services and the Arizona Biomedical Research Commission.

Data from the Living Brain Project available upon request at AD Knowledge Portal. Samples associated with psychiatric diseases or drug abuse were excluded. Only samples with an RNA integrity number (RIN) ≥ 6 were retained for analysis. Data collection for LBP was funded by the National Institute of Aging (R01AG069976) and the Michael J. Fox Foundation.

The RNA-seq data generated in this study have been deposited with links to BioProject accession number PRJNA1287059 in the NCBI BioProject database. Libraries were sequenced in a NovaSeq-6000 (Illumina Inc.), generating a minimum of 100 million paired-end 150 nt reads. Reads were aligned to the GRCm39 genome using STAR v2.7.1 with GENCODE M36 annotation.

dataset_identifier: Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center Proteomic Cohort
dataset_context_from_paper: Proteomic data from the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center cohort used to develop and validate the GPND-AI classifier for neurodegenerative disease classification. The study identified a 15-protein panel that accurately classifies individuals across four major neurodegenerative diseases. Data can be requested through the Knight ADRC data request form.

The 15-protein panel was validated against neuropathology-confirmed diagnoses. Data can be requested by contacting the corresponding author.

Summary statistics resource used for genome-wide association analysis of Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia. The resource provides access to GWAS summary statistics for genetic variant analysis.

Protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis using the STRING database was performed to determine the functional interactome of genes near genome-wide significant and suggestive loci associated with ACD and VaD. Analysis comprised 82 ACD and 21 VaD GW significant and suggestive genes. Evidence of interaction between proteins was based on experiments, co-occurrence, database, and co-expression with a minimum score of 0.15.

Population-based cohort of adults aged 65+ years residing in an under-resourced small-town region of the United States recruited by age-stratified random sampling from voter registration lists. Over approximately two years, a total of 2036 individuals were enrolled. Baseline and annual neuropsychological assessment battery included tests of five cognitive domains: memory (Logical Memory, Visual Reproduction, Face Name Associate, Fuld Object Memory), language (Boston Naming, Category Fluency for names of animals, Indiana University Token), attention/processing speed (Trail making Test A Time, Digit Span), executive function (Trail making Test B Time, Fluency for initial letters, Clock Drawing), and visuospatial function (Block Design, Benton Visual Form Discrimination). Participants were screened using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) with standard adjustment for age and education. Participants scoring ≥21 underwent detailed assessment which was repeated annually. The study examined memory outcomes and the impact of surgery over time, with analyses stratified by case/control status.

The social media posts used in this study are publicly available and do not contain protected health information (PHI). The study used annotated Reddit posts as the source for generating synthetic clinical notes, ensuring that no real PHI from clinical notes is used. These publicly available mental health datasets were leveraged to curate synthetic clinical notes for training NLP models on downstream tasks such as entity recognition and concept extraction.

Synthetic clinical notes generated from annotated Reddit posts were created and used for training NLP models. The study notes that synthetic notes are the most homogeneous, reflecting the templated and repetitive nature of generated documentation. The synthetic data generation method demonstrates strong alignment with real-world data in terms of contextual fidelity, structural coherence, and readability, though they remain limited by low diversity in the source of data.

Mayo notes were used as a reference dataset showing unexpectedly high diversity across multiple dimensions in lexical and semantic richness. Clinical notes vary considerably in their lexical and semantic richness, with Mayo notes demonstrating this variation. The study indicates that models trained on synthetic notes may fail to generalize to more linguistically and semantically diverse corpora such as Mayo notes.

The authors constructed the RNAs in Blood of AD (RBAD) repository to provide a centralized database comprising AD-associated peripheral biomarkers and features related to AD development. Processed data are available online at http://www.bioinform.cn/RBAD/. The repository includes bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, and Clinical panels displaying only protein-coding genes presented as publication-quality figures via a user-friendly and login-free website.

Plasma proteome data from Hubei Memory & Aging Cohort Study (HMACS) were analyzed using the Limma package. The study was approved by the ethics committee at Wuhan University of Science and Technology (protocol code: 201845; approved on October 22, 2018). Written informed consents were obtained from all participants, or in the case of cognitively impaired persons, from a proxy. Proteomic data from HMACS individuals are available from the corresponding author upon responsible request due to privacy or ethical restrictions.
The Genotype-Tissue Expression Project (GTEx) database was used to verify the tissue and cell-type specificity of genes identified in the study.
The Human Protein Atlas (HPA) database was used to verify the tissue and cell-type specificity of genes identified in the study.

dataset_identifier: Amyloid Biomarker Study data pooling initiative
dataset_context_from_paper: Data for this cross-sectional study were obtained from the Amyloid Biomarker Study data pooling initiative (January 1, 2012, to the present [data collection is ongoing]), including 95 studies. The study selected all participants for whom information on age, cognitive status, amyloid status, and presence of CMBs was available, with a maximum interval of 1 year between CMB and amyloid assessments. This resulted in the inclusion of 4080 participants from 15 research and memory clinic studies (992 were excluded due to missing information on CMBs). A total of 2973 participants were in the CU group and 1107 participants were in the MCI-ADD group. Information on number of APOE ε4 alleles was available for 2513 participants (84.5%) in the CU group and 890 (80.4%) in the MCI-ADD group.

Data from 1,654 participants (916 males, 738 females; average ages 65.8 and 65.9, respectively) from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) with FTLD-related syndromes including behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), Primary Progressive Aphasia (non-fluent variant (nfvPPA), semantic variant (svPPA)), Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP). Participants' symptoms were assessed using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI). Prevalence ratios and odds ratios were computed to assess the likelihood of NPS comorbidities when agitation was present in males and females. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was performed to identify NPS associated with agitation and how they varied by sex.

data_repository: ARTFL-LEFFTDS Longitudinal Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Study
dataset_context_from_paper: Data from 1,654 participants (916 males, 738 females; average ages 65.8 and 65.9, respectively) from the ARTFL-LEFFTDS Longitudinal Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration (ALLFTD) study with FTLD-related syndromes: behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD), Primary Progressive Aphasia (non-fluent variant (nfvPPA), semantic variant (svPPA)), Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP). Participants' symptoms were assessed using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI) to investigate sex differences in agitation across FTLD-related syndromes and its relationship to various neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS).

Raw data from ALLFTD study available upon reasonable request with formal applications. Data requests can be completed via ALLFTD at https://www.allftd.org/data. 4RTNI data requests can be completed via ALLFTD at https://www.allftd.org/data. Cross-cohort validation analyses used independent cohort of sporadic PSP-RS and controls from 4RTNI using SomaScan platform for protein quantification.

Data from the UCSF Memory and Aging Center can be requested via UCSF at https://memory.ucsf.edu/research-trials/professional/open-science. Raw data available upon reasonable request with formal applications. Certain data elements may be restricted due to the potential for identifiability in the context of the sensitive nature of the genetic data.

For BioFINDER 2 data, anonymized data will be shared by request from a qualified academic investigator as long as data transfer is in agreement with European Union legislation on the general data protection regulation and decisions by the Ethical Review Board of Sweden and Region Skåne, which should be regulated in a material transfer agreement. Cross-cohort validation analyses reconstructed genetic FTLD modules in independent cohort of FTLD, AD and controls using Olink platform.
Publicly available summary statistics from Dammer et al. can be accessed via the supplementary materials for the respective publication.
Publicly available summary statistics from Rutledge et al. can be accessed via the supplementary materials for the respective publication.

Algorithms used for protein data processing and analysis are available in existing R packages and via GitHub at https://github.com/edammer, as described in the Methods. A total of 4,138 proteins were quantified and organized into modules of protein co-expression using WGCNA.

Population-based cohort study (n=111, median age 76 IQR: 72-80, 54% female) from a medically and economically-depressed Rust Belt area of southwestern Pennsylvania. Participants underwent plasma p-tau217 measurement using assays from the University of Pittsburgh, ALZpath Inc., and NULISA from Alamar Biosciences. Aβ imaging was performed with 11C-PiB, where global Aβ+ was defined using a threshold of 1.346 SUVR. Primary analysis using ALZpath p-tau217 reported PPV of 0.6, NPV of 0.92, sensitivity of 0.82, and specificity of 0.80. Secondary analyses using UPitt p-tau217 and NULISA p-tau217 assays showed PPV: 0.56-0.60, NPV: 0.89-0.93.

Human Connectome Project population-based cohort (n=229, median age 62 IQR: 56-70, 65% female) of self-identified Black and non-Hispanic Whites in Pittsburgh city. Plasma p-tau217 was measured using assays from the University of Pittsburgh, ALZpath Inc., and NULISA from Alamar Biosciences. Aβ imaging was performed with 11C-PiB, where global Aβ+ was defined using a threshold of 1.346 SUVR. Primary analysis in HCP showed PPV of 0.40 and NPV of 0.97, with sensitivity of 0.85 and specificity of 0.78. Secondary analysis using UPitt p-tau217 performed comparably (PPV: 0.38 and NPV: 0.97).

Longitudinal cohort study of cognitively normal older adults from a medically- and economically-underserved Rust Belt region of Western Pennsylvania, USA. Baseline cohort included 111 participants (median age 76.7 years, 54.1% female, 16.2% APOE ε4 carriers). Follow-up cohort of 65 participants assessed at two-year follow-up (median age 77.7 years, 50.8% female, 18.5% APOE ε4 carriers). Plasma biomarkers measured at baseline (n=111) and two-year follow-up (n=65) including Aβ42/40, p-tau181, p-tau231, p-tau217, NfL, and GFAP. Neuroimaging assessments included Aβ PET using [11C]PiB and tau PET using [18F]AV-1451. Cognitive status assessed using Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) with only cognitively normal participants included (CDR=0). Study evaluated associations between plasma biomarkers and brain amyloid-beta and tau pathology in cognitively normal older adults.

887 individuals in the Bio-Hermes Study (Global Alzheimer's Platform Foundation) completed Cognivue Clarity, amyloid PET, and pTau217. The cohort had a mean age of 71.8 ± 6.7y, 15.5 ± 2.7y of education, 56.4% female, 37.3% ApoE e4 carriers, and was 78.8% non-Hispanic White. The clinical-pathological diagnoses were 297 True Controls, 91 Preclinical AD, 111 MCI-AD, 171 MCI-non-AD, 130 AD dementia, and 87 non-AD dementia. The 4-level Cognivue Amyloid Risk Measure (CARM) was derived using a machine learning paradigm. Amyloid PET SUVR and pTau217 levels were significantly different by Cognivue Clarity thresholds. Amyloid positivity increased across the 4 CARM thresholds.

An AD test-retest cohort (N = 10x2) was used to assess within-subject repeatability of Centiloid (CL) quantification across seven pipelines. Test-retest analysis revealed absolute biases <5 CL, within-subject coefficients of variation 2.6-4.4% and 95% repeatability coefficients 8.1-16.1 CL.

An amnestic MCI cohort (N = 80) was used to assess reproducibility in terms of absolute agreement in continuous CL values. Agreement in +/- status between software was 92-99% (kappa 0.84-0.97) in this dataset. Strong group-level associations in continuous CL estimates were observed across pairs of software (R2 ≥0.93).

Cases from the BioFINDER-1 cohort enriched for amyloid loads around published positivity thresholds (0-50CL) (N = 110) were used to assess reliability for dichotomizing amyloid scans into positive and negative at three thresholds of 11, 25 and 37 CL. Inter-software reliability in dichotomization was >92% for scans across a wide range of CL values, but the percentage was lower for scans with amyloid loads closer to the range of typical positivity thresholds.

Data used in these analyses are available through standard application procedures described on the BIOCARD website (www.biocard-se.org). The BIOCARD Study consists of 7 Cores and two Projects including Administrative Core, Clinical Core, Imaging Core, Biospecimen Core, Informatics Core, Biostatistics Core, and Neuropathology Core. The study includes genotyping of the APOE gene performed via restriction enzyme digestion of PCR-amplified genomic DNA, with participants classified as ε4 carriers if they had at least one copy of the ε4 allele.

Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium (GNPC, https://www.neuroproteome.org/), launched in 2023, is a mega consortium combining multiple dementia and population cohorts, including health aging, Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and stroke/TIA. The latest GNPC v1.3 release collected 20,426 participants from 22 contributors (sites), 3,942 of whom had longitudinal visits. Baseline visit proteomics data was used for model development. GNPC will be open-access upon the publication of this study.

Pseudonymized BioFINDER-2 data will be shared by request from a qualified academic investigator for the sole purpose of replicating procedures and results presented in the article and as long as data transfer is in agreement with EU legislation on the general data protection regulation and decisions by the Swedish Ethical Review Authority and Region Skåne. BioFINDER-2 has 32 embedding dimensions and was used for model generalization and validation in the ProtAIDe-Dx model development.

PHASE–AD is trained on MRI scans from 8,415 participants and robustly captures limbic-predominant and hippocampal-sparing atrophy subtypes that were identified across seven independent datasets. Two cross-validation schemes revealed high robustness across different field strength and scanner manufacturer configurations.

PHASE–AD robustly captures limbic-predominant and hippocampal-sparing atrophy subtypes that were identified across seven independent datasets. Atrophy classifications were associated with diverging clinical profiles and tau accumulation patterns. In prospective designs mirroring contemporary AD trials, they stratified longitudinal cognitive trajectories and outperformed semi-quantitative visual MRI assessments.

The study involves analysis of FUS protein expression and localization in Drosophila, including fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) experiments measuring nuclear protein dynamics with recovery half-time of 30.35 s ± 7.97 s (SD) from n = 11 nuclei from 3 animals, and experiments combining mGFP-FUS expression with endogenously C-terminally flag-tagged Polr2A subunit.

eQTL data from BrainMeta version 2 cis-eQTL used in SMR analysis to evaluate whether expression of ten TNF-pathway genes have a causal effect on PD and RBD traits. Significant cis-eQTLs (p ≤ 5 × 10⁻⁸) were selected based on their location within or near each gene, using cis-window thresholds of ±500 kb. eQTL data from caudate, cortex, substantia nigra tissues were analyzed.

Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) version 8 cis-eQTL summary statistics used in SMR analysis to evaluate causal effects of TNF-pathway gene expression on PD and RBD traits. Significant cis-eQTLs (p ≤ 5 × 10⁻⁸) were selected and HEIDI test was used to distinguish true causal effects from those due to linkage. eQTL data from whole blood tissue were analyzed.
GWAS summary statistics for PD progression trait used in the study. Summary statistics for the PD motor progression trait can be downloaded from the PD Progression Meta-GWAS Browser.
Summary statistics for the PD motor progression trait available via Zenodo with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8017385.

Data from the AMP PD Knowledge Platform used in the preparation of this article. Variants were restricted to biallelic sites with sufficient depth of coverage (DP ≥ 25) and low genotype missingness (missingness <0.05).

UK Biobank data accessed via NeuroHub used in the study. For UKB data, variants were restricted to biallelic sites with sufficient depth of coverage (DP ≥ 25) and low genotype missingness (missingness <0.05).

dataset_identifier: McGill, PPMI, APDGC, IPDGC, NINDS, NGRC, UKB cohorts
dataset_context_from_paper: Genotyping data from 7 cohorts used for PRS pathway analysis: McGill, Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI), Autopsy-Confirmed Parkinson Disease GWAS Consortium (APDGC) (dbGaP phs000394.v1.p1), International Parkinson's Disease Genomics Consortium (IPDGC) NeuroX dataset (dbGap phs000918.v1.p1), National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) Genome-wide genotyping in Parkinson's disease (dbGap phs000089.v4.p2), NeuroGenetics Research Consortium (NGRC) (dbGap phs000196.v3.p1) and UKB. Effect size estimates were derived from the most recent largest European PD GWAS.

Large genetic dataset from the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium (ADGC) used to assess the association of rs2288911 with CAA and AD risk. Authors leveraged established pipelines and state-of-the-art APOE genotype quality control to ensure accurate assessment of genetic associations conditioned on APOE *4 and APOE *2. Specific data repositories and identifiers for ADGC data are indicated in Table.S1 of the supplement.

Large genetic dataset from the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP) used to replicate the rs2288911-CAA association and assess AD risk. Authors reproduced the CAA finding in NACC data overlapping ADGC and ADSP. Specific data repositories and identifiers for ADSP data are indicated in Table.S1 of the supplement.

Population-based genetic dataset from UK Biobank (UKB) used to assess the association of rs2288911 with CAA and AD risk alongside ADGC and ADSP data. Authors leveraged this large genetic dataset with established pipelines and APOE genotype quality control.
Dataset used to reproduce the Fujita et al. rs2288911*T-CAA association. Authors successfully reproduced the CAA finding in ROSMAP data as part of their replication strategy.

Dataset overlapping with ADGC and ADSP used to replicate the rs2288911-CAA association. Authors reproduced the CAA finding in NACC data overlapping ADGC and ADSP, effectively validating the association.
Population-based dataset (n=801) used as an additional replication attempt for the rs2288911-CAA association. The effect direction was consistent but diminished and non-significant in this cohort.

Microglia eQTL dataset from Fujita et al. 2024 available from the AMP-AD knowledge portal / Synapse. This dataset inspired the authors to look at the association of rs2288911 with CAA and AD risk in large genetic datasets.
Microglia eQTL dataset from Kosoy et al. 2022 available from the AMP-AD knowledge portal / Synapse, used in the context of Alzheimer's disease research.
