DNA was obtained from blood samples of the ALFA parent cohort through a salting-out protocol. In total, 2686 participants were genotyped. Genotyping was performed with the Illumina Infinium Neuro Consortium (NeuroChip) Array (build GRCh37/hg19). Quality control procedure was performed using PLINK software. Imputation was performed using the Michigan Imputation Server with the haplotype Reference Consortium Panel (HRC r1.1 2016). After the corresponding quality control procedure, 2527 individuals remained with available genotype data. Genetic predisposition to AD was assessed using polygenic risk scoring through PRSice version 2. The AD polygenic score (PRS_AD) was calculated by selecting representative genetic variants per linkage disequilibrium (LD) block with an LD threshold of r2 >0.1 within a 250-kb window.

Bioassay datasets derived from compound IDs (CIDs), structure IDs (SIDs), and targets were used to develop machine learning models. These models were built using algorithms from the scikit-learn Python library. Data are curated to the C-Surv ontology to ensure comparability across diverse datasets and to provide standardised categorisation for metadata tools.

dataset_context_from_paper: The datasets generated and analyzed during the current study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. The study involved competitive immunohistochemistry (IHC) assays performed on post-mortem Alzheimer's disease brain tissue to test binding of lecanemab and donanemab to amyloid-beta plaques. Displacement was assessed by comparing the staining of 6E10, mAb158, and mDona on tissue sections with and without co- or pre-incubation of excess lecanemab or donanemab. Staining intensity was quantified using ImageJ with a threshold-based approach to identify pixels with positive labeling. Results showed statistically significant reductions in 6E10 staining intensity with lecanemab co-incubation (100% vs 39 ± 7.6%, p = 0.03) and pre-incubation (100% vs 19.7 ± 2.6%, p = 0.001).

UCSC tracks used to compile the medulloblastoma dataset. These tracks were accessed to obtain chromatin synthesis and regulatory element data for the analysis of differentially methylated regions (DMRs) and transcription factor binding sites (TFBS).

UCSC tracks used to compile the medulloblastoma dataset. Transcription factor binding site (TFBS) conservation data was used to identify and analyze TFBS enrichments within DMR-associated promoters. Enrichments were calculated by comparing TFBS counts in DMR-associated promoters to background RefSeq promoters overlapped by 450K probes.

The 450K array was used as the primary source for CpG methylation data. A background set of 461,272 autosomal CpGs from the 450K array was used for enrichment testing. DMR enrichments in specific genomic features were tested by comparing proportions of DMR-CpGs to the overlap of features with this background CpG list. The 450K CpG set also served as the map file for INRICH analysis of DMR overlaps with histone marks.

dataset_identifier: ENCODE and REMC histone mark datasets
dataset_context_from_paper: ENCODE and REMC curated histone mark datasets were used as target regions in INRICH analysis to test enrichment of DMRs overlapping these regulatory marks. DMRs (hyper and hypo considered separately) were tested as test regions against histone marks, with the 450K CpG background set used as the map file. Empirical P-values were estimated based on 10,000 permutations to determine if DMRs overlap histone marks more than expected by chance.

RefSeq promoters were used as a background list for TFBS enrichment calculations. All RefSeq promoters overlapped by sampled 450K probes were compared against DMR-associated promoters. RefSeq gene annotations were also used for genomic feature annotation, with promoter annotations given precedence when DMRs overlapped both promoters and gene bodies.

dataset_identifier: GWAS SNP associations with Alzheimer's Disease
dataset_context_from_paper: GWAS SNPs associated with Alzheimer's Disease (AD) were used to identify DMRs occurring within 250 kb of AD-associated variants. SNPs within DMRs exhibiting strong linkage disequilibrium (LD) with AD GWAS hits and brain eQTLs were identified and analyzed for their potential regulatory roles.

Brain expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) were used to identify SNPs within DMRs that exhibit strong LD with AD GWAS hits. These eQTLs were analyzed to determine which genes' expression is influenced by identified regulatory variants within the identified DMRs.

The original data used in this manuscript are available for download in the ADNI database. The dataset was used to develop machine learning models for classification of individuals with mild cognitive impairment (sMCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) from healthy controls (HC) using blood-based biomarkers including metabolomic profiling. The study analyzed analytes across amino acids, lipoproteins, and fatty acids categories, with key predictive features including APOE ε4 genotype, leucine, branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), valine, low-density lipoprotein particle diameter, omega-6 to omega-3 fatty acid ratios, and various other metabolites for binary classification tasks.

Publicly available miRNA expression datasets used to test the NormiRazor approach. The study tested on 8 datasets containing subsets of GSE68314 with 50 to 400 miRNAs. The authors evaluated execution times for three normalization algorithms (geNorm, BestKeeper, and NormFinder) on these datasets, achieving speedup factors of 18.7 ±0.6, 104.7 ±4.2, and 76.5 ±2.2 times respectively compared to previous Python implementation.

Chromatin accessibility (ATAC) metrics computed per barcode included transcription start site (TSS) enrichment, n ATAC, nucleosome signal, percent reads in peaks, fraction of reads overlapping promoter regions, and fraction of reads overlapping ENCODE blacklist regions (Supplementary Fig. 15-18).

dataset_context_from_paper: To identify cell types, we used the Seurat label transfer functions FindTransferAnchors and TransferData with 30 principal components, using single-cell data published by Kanton et al. as the reference data set with the following modifications: astrocytes and microglia were removed from the reference prior to label transfer, and after label transfer all cells with 'Glyc' (glycolysis) labels were removed from our data set.

Single-cell gene expression was quantified using CellRanger (10X Genomics). Single cells were filtered based on the following criteria: at least 500 genes expressed, at least 2000 UMI counts over all genes, and less than 15% mitochondrial gene expression. Gene expression was normalized using NormalizeExpression in Seurat. The multiplexed libraries were pooled and sequenced on Illumina Novaseq X Plus sequencer with 100 cycle kits using the following read length: 28 bp Read1 for cell barcode and UMI, and 90 bp Read2 for transcript. The single cell library preparation and sequencing was done at Northwestern University NUseq facility core.

Data from the CALERIE trial are available from the Aging Research Biobank and the CALERIE Biorepository. DNAm data for CALERIE were processed at Duke University and used to develop aging biomarkers through machine learning methods.

Cell assay data analyzing the replication ability of MSA prions with various α-synuclein mutations (V55Y, V66F, G36K, A30P, E46K, A53T) across multiple cell lines. A heat map was created showing cell infection relative to the average of control samples for each patient sample on every cell line tested (Table 4). The study investigated how specific mutations affect MSA strain biology and α-synuclein misfolding using both cell-based assays and protein modeling.

dataset_identifier: PDB structures from Goedert and Scheres labs
dataset_context_from_paper: Cryo-EM structures of α-synuclein in MSA and Lewy body (LB) diseases determined by Goedert and Scheres labs. These structures were used as the basis for protein modeling to develop hypotheses about the effect of specific mutations on MSA replication. The structures revealed distinct conformations between MSA and PD strains and contained pockets with unknown non-protein densities that could not be accounted for in calculations.

Protein expression profile dataset downloaded from the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus. Generated by the Invitrogen ProtoArray V5.0 platform. Dataset was used for identifying differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and included in machine learning model with AUC evaluation.

Global miRNA expression profiles were obtained from two publicly accessible Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets: GSE46579 and GSE48552. The former dataset contains blood miRNA expression data from 48 AD patients and 22 controls. The dataset used Illumina HiSeq 2000 platform. This dataset was used to investigate biological significance of genes positioned at the intersection of AD and IR pathways by analyzing miRNA expression profiles.

Global miRNA expression profiles were obtained from two publicly accessible Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets: GSE46579 and GSE48552. The latter dataset contains miRNA expression data of 6 AD patients and 6 controls from their prefrontal cortex. The dataset used Illumina HiSeq 2000 platform. This dataset was used to investigate biological significance of genes positioned at the intersection of AD and IR pathways by analyzing miRNA expression profiles.

Social workers gathered structured data in REDCap to assess participant eligibility, including detailed questions regarding health and family history, availability of a study partner, ability to complete study procedures including biomarker studies, and exclusion criteria. Data collection took place from August 2023 to June 2024. When participants spontaneously asked about compensation, this was recorded in REDCap.

Bulk (n = 632) and single-cell nuclei transcriptomic profiling (n = 427) of the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) from the Religious Order Study/Memory Aging Project (ROSMAP). These transcriptomic datasets were used to determine mechanisms of cellular senescence in postmortem brain samples, revealing upregulation of cellular senescence signatures in AD brain tissues across different cell types in comparison with controls. Single cell nuclei transcriptomics identified strong correlation between arachidonic acid (AA) activation and P2RY12 (homeostatic) microglia (P<0.0001), and association with worse cognitive performance and AD neuropathology.

Lipidomic profiling was performed on a subset of 200 brains from the midfrontal cortex of ROS. Lipidomic analysis of postmortem brain tissues confirmed activation of arachidonic acid (AA) derived eicosanoids and implicated the activation of calcium dependent phospholipase A2 (cPLA2).

Eight pseudobulked scRNA-seq case-control datasets comprising 4,256,380 cells from 682 donors across five tissues — brain (ad_brain, pd_brain), blood (covid_blood, sle_blood), kidney (ckd_kidney), lung (covid_lung, ipf_lung), and heart (dcm_heart) — yielding 5,923 pseudobulk samples and 1,864 pathway-level comparisons per method across 10 Reactome pathways. All counts were aggregated by uniform pseudobulk summation followed by log2 counts-per-million (CPM) transformation. These datasets were used to evaluate five pathway activity scoring methods (ssGSEA, GSVA, z-score, AUCell, UCell) against five criteria: biological relevance, aggregation stability, outlier sensitivity, normalization stability, and sample-size stability.

PathwayBench code, ground-truth pathway sets, evaluation scripts, and figure-generation scripts archived at Zenodo (release v3.1). To reproduce the analysis, clone the repository at tag v3.1 and unpack the data archive into the repository root.
Supporting data — pseudobulk expression matrices, per-dataset pathway scores, evaluation outputs, and rank-window simulation data — are deposited at Zenodo.

Metadata fields and controlled vocabularies from the metadata-schemas GitHub repository were converted into formal, machine-readable data models using LinkML tools, and shared in the public GitHub repository: https://github.com/brain-bican/models. Provenance components were added to the LinkML schemas to align with the entity-centric, biospecimen provenance data models. These formal schemas serve several critical functions: (i) validation of incoming data, (ii) transformation of heterogeneous data into a consistent representation, and (iii) enabling interoperability of data across downstream tools and platforms.

The scrattch.taxonomy library (RRID:SCR_027910; https://alleninstitute.github.io/scrattch.mapping) provides a single function that creates an AIT file for users when provided basic single-cell transcriptomics data and metadata files (buildTaxonomy), along with other functions for standardizing metadata, predicting ontology terms from text values, and defining taxonomy modes.

The sample of the study was defined by 429 CU middle-aged participants at risk of AD from the ALFA+ nested cohort with available information on genetics, brain imaging markers and cognitive data. A subset of them had information at two-time points (N=367). Genetic predisposition for clinical AD (PRSAD and PRSADnoAPOE) and AD pathology (PRSAβ42-CSF and PRSpTau-CSF) were calculated. The study assessed the association between each PRS and global amyloid PET deposition expressed in Centiloids, AD Dickerson MRI-signature, hippocampal volume and cognitive outcomes, at baseline and rate of change over visits. PET and MRI outcomes were defined as the annual rate of change over a 3-year period in cognitively unimpaired middle-aged individuals.

The miRNA sequencing data of 112 subjects have been submitted to the NCBI GEO repository with the accession number GSE215789. The clinical information is not publicly available due to restrictions imposed by the Belgian/Dutch legislation on the protection of personal data. This dataset was used as the internal validation dataset for evaluating CSF biomarker-associated miRNAs as classifiers in AD cases vs controls, in MCI cases vs controls, and in AD cases vs MCI cases.

The RT-qPCR dataset used in the external validation is a publicly available dataset that can be found at the GEO with GSE90828, doi: 10.1186/s40364–016–0076–1 (2016). This dataset was used for external validation of the miRNA findings from the primary sequencing study.

From the experimentally validated miRNA-target interaction database miRTarBase (release 9.0), 92 all gene targets of CSF biomarker-associated miRNAs were retrieved; only interactions determined by the 'strong evidence' validation method including reporter assay, Western blot, Northern blot, and qPCR were included.

Mass spectrometry proteomics data deposited to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository. Spectral data were processed in Spectronaut (Biognosys v19.5) against the UniProt Homo sapiens reference proteome (UP000005640, release 2025) using the directDIA workflow. A 1% precursor and protein-level q-value cutoff was applied, with decoys generated for FDR control. Protein inference was performed with the IDPicker algorithm, using MS2-level quantification and median peptide/precursor intensities. Protein MS2 intensity values were assessed for quality using ProteiNorm. The data were normalized using VSN and analyzed using proteoDA to perform statistical analysis using Linear Models for Microarray Data (limma package) with empirical Bayes smoothing.

Extended Data table listing proteins identified by proteomic analysis and their differential expression between experimental groups. For each protein, the table includes gene symbols, log2 fold change values, and p-values used for differential expression analysis.

dataset_identifier: Not specified - metabolomics and biomarker data
dataset_context_from_paper: Raw metabolomics and biomarker data will be shared with qualified investigators using the request form. The metabolomics data was generated by a metabolomics core supported by the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences grant-5UL1TR001873. Data includes metabolic features analyzed through WGCNA modules significantly associated with outcomes, with annotations made using an internal library and the Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) via xMSannotator. Chemical class enrichment was determined using MetaboAnalyst. Pathway analysis was conducted using the 'functional analysis' module in MetaboAnalyst (version 5.0) with mummichog algorithm and human MFN reference database, with results presented for pathways with Fisher's exact test p-value < 0.3.

Human Metabolome Database (HMDB) was used for matching and annotating metabolic features. Annotations were made by matching to HMDB using the R package xMSannotator (version 1.3.2). Enrichment analysis was performed using HMDBIDs for features with an annotation confidence score < 3.

The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) is a large-scale repository that tracks neurodegenerative progression from mild cognitive impairment to AD through integrated longitudinal markers. The neuroimaging data from ADNI were analyzed in this study to identify shared structural principles in neurodegenerative diseases using transductive, unsupervised domain adaptation logic. ADNI data collection and sharing was funded by the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (National Institutes of Health Grant U01 AG024904) and DOD ADNI (Department of Defense award number W81XWH-12-2-0012). These datasets are available to researchers upon registration and approval of a data utility request through the consortium portal.

The Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) is a comprehensive multi-modal dataset spanning idiopathic and genetic PD cases alongside cognitively normal (CN) individuals. The neuroimaging data from PPMI were analyzed in this study to identify shared structural principles in neurodegenerative diseases using the entire disease-specific manifold to maximize statistical resolution and identify common pathological laws. PPMI is a public-private partnership funded by the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research and funding partners. These datasets are available to researchers upon registration and approval of a data utility request through the consortium portal.

Generation Scotland cohort data was used as the primary training dataset for building weighted linear predictors of CRP from genome-wide DNAm (N = 17,936). The training dataset included all CpG sites available in GS to document relationships between local and global DNAm variation and CRP blood levels. Three prediction methods were applied: elastic net regression, Bayesian penalised regression, and PCA combined with elastic net regression. Data access requires review by the GS Access Committee with applications to access@generationscotland.org.

ALSPAC cohort data was used as a test cohort and included in the training space restricted to CpG sites common to EPIC and 450K arrays (n = 374,785 sites following quality control). The cohort was part of the external validation for DNAm prediction models of CRP. Data access is through managed open access with submissions directed to alspac-data@bristol.ac.uk.

SABRE cohort data was used as an external test cohort for validating DNAm prediction models. The cohort was included in the restricted training space of CpG sites common across arrays (n = 374,785 sites). Data access requests should be directed to mrclha.swiftinfo@ucl.ac.uk.

Lothian Birth Cohort data was used as an external test cohort included in the restricted training space of CpG sites common across arrays (n = 374,785 sites). The cohort was part of external validation for DNAm prediction models of CRP. Data access requests can be made through the provided information portal.

HELIOS cohort was held as a further external test cohort to understand how missing CpG sites would impact prediction. HELIOS did not contain 193 of the 374,785 common CpG sites. Data access request proposals should be directed to helios_science@ntu.edu.sg for consideration by the HELIOS Study's principal investigators.
1000 Genomes Phase 3 dataset was used as a reference resource in the study, referenced in the deposited data table as a resource for genomic analysis.

Epigenome-wide association statistics from linear models are available via the EWAS Catalog and Zenodo. Epigenome-wide association statistics from Bayesian penalised regression are also available at this location. These summary statistics represent the results of EWAS analyses performed in the study.

Epigenome-wide association statistics from Bayesian penalised regression are available at the University of Edinburgh Datashare site. CpGs and weights derived from elastic net regression, Bayesian penalised regression and the combined PCA and elastic net regression strategies are made available at the Edinburgh Datashare site. CpGs and weights for elastic net regression and 'PCA+elnet'-based approaches are available in Tables S11 and S12.

All original code used in the manuscript has been deposited at Zenodo. This includes code for elastic net regression, Bayesian penalised regression, and PCA combined with elastic net regression methods used to build weighted linear predictors of CRP from genome-wide DNAm.

dataset_identifier: Not publicly available - available from corresponding author upon request
dataset_context_from_paper: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. Study includes immunoblot analysis of protein levels (Cleaved-Caspase3, GAPDH loading control) in cardiac lysates from WT and Tg2576 mice (n=5 vs. n=4 and n=4 samples), immunofluorescence imaging of collagen type I fibers (COL1A1), Aβ, and Cleaved-Caspase3 in cardiac sections from WT and Tg2576 mice. Protein bands were detected using Odyssey CLx Imaging System and quantified with Image Studio Lite Software.

RNA sequencing data files can be accessed at GEO Accession Number GSE299976 and the Alzheimer's Disease Workbench (ADWB). The RNA sequencing data were aligned to GRCh38 reference genome using STAR v2.7.3a and analyzed using MAJIQ (v2.1) to identify cryptic splicing events with a threshold of 10% difference in percent spliced in (PSI, ΔΨ). The data was used to assess TDP-43 expression hits and identify significant genes through enrichment analysis using clusterProfiler, GOstats, enrich.HGT, and GSEA packages.

Mass spectrometry proteomics data have been deposited to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository with the dataset identifier PXD063206. Proteomic raw data were analyzed using MaxQuant software (v. 1.6.14) with a reviewed Swiss-Prot Homo sapiens database and custom neuron-specific contaminant FASTA library. Protein intensities from protein.txt output files were used for nonSILAC data analysis, and dSILAC data was analyzed using a previously established workflow with Lys8/Arg10 as the heavy channel.

The zebrafish gliovascular single-cell dataset can be accessed at NCBI's Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) with the accession number GSE225721. This dataset was generated from zebrafish experiments and used in the analysis alongside brain tissue and whole genome sequencing data to study Alzheimer's disease genetics.

Whole Genome Sequencing data (WGS) from EFIGA and NIA-AD FBS cohorts that were analyzed in the study have been deposited to NIAGADS (The National Institute on Aging Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site) and are shared with the research community as part of the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP). WGS was performed at the New York Genome Center using 1 µg of DNA with Illumina PCR-free library protocol and sequencing on the Illumina HiSeq platform. Genomes were sequenced to a mean coverage of 30×. The EFIGA families (n = 307) were harmonized and jointly called variants to create a uniform analysis set.

Case–control, family-based, and longitudinal AD genetic cohorts were available through public repositories, with genetic data from high-density single-nucleotide polymorphism microarrays, exome microarrays, whole-exome (WES) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). These data pertained to cohorts belonging to the ADGC and the ADSP R3. ADGC and ADSP genetic data underwent extensive quality control, imputation to the TOPMed reference panel (for ADGC array-based samples), and ancestry determination.
Population-based data from the UKB was additionally used, where researchers had access to health record information to derive case–control diagnoses for Alzheimer's disease genetic analysis.

The brain tissue used in this analysis was requested from the New York Brain Bank at Columbia University. Raw data generated from the brain tissue and zebrafish experiments are available upon request.

Data were obtained from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database. The ADNI is a longitudinal multicentre observational study that provides a comprehensive and widely used collection of longitudinal clinical, imaging, genetic, and other biomarker data. All data from this study could be obtained from the ADNI database. The study includes measurements of APOEε4, BMI, cerebral microbleeds, cerebral small vessel disease markers, lipid profiles (HDL-C, LDL-C, triglycerides), lipid-modifying agents use, and white matter hyperintensities. ADNI data are disseminated by the Laboratory for Neuro Imaging at the University of Southern California.

Cell type annotations for all the functional categories were created using plink format.bed/.bim/.fam filesets of 1000 Genomes Phase 3 for European population and LD scores were computed based on a 1 centiMorgan (cM) window. Since the annotations were built on top of the baseline model, 1000 Genomes Phase 3 was used together with the HapMap3 SNPs.

To prevent bias from variable imputation quality both between and within each GWAS study, all the GWAS SNPs were filtered to HapMap3 SNPs, as these SNPs are well imputed in most studies. Since the annotations were built on top of the baseline model, 1000 Genomes Phase 3 was used together with the HapMap3 SNPs.

dataset_identifier: PLAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq, H3K4me3 ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq datasets
dataset_context_from_paper: PLAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq, H3K4me3 ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq datasets were taken from (1) and processed data is available: https://github.com/nottalexi/brain-cell-type-peak-files. Cell type disease enrichment by sLDSC regression was assessed using chromatin interactions defined as (i) all PLAC-seq bins irrespective of functional genomic annotations (total PLAC-seq bins), (ii) PLAC-seq bins subset to both active gene promoters (H3K4me3 + H3K27ac) and distal enhancers (H3K27ac only) (promoter & enhancer PLAC-seq bins), (iii) PLAC-seq bins subset to active gene promoters (promoter PLAC-seq bins) and (iv) PLAC-seq bins subset to distal enhancers (enhancer PLAC-seq bins).
Cell type disease enrichment was assessed using summary statistics from two complementary AD GWAS; one study was based exclusively on clinical diagnosis.
Cell type disease enrichment was assessed using summary statistics from two complementary AD GWAS; the second included by-proxy cases.

The Accelerating Medicines Partnership (AMP-AD) data in this manuscript are available via the AD Knowledge Portal. Gene read counts and metadata files of three RNA-Seq cohorts were downloaded from AD knowledge portal on Synapse, each consisting of postmortem brains from AD and controls. These included the Mayo Clinic temporal cortex (Mayo-TCX), Mount Sinai VA Medical Center Brain Bank superior temporal gyrus (MSBB-BM22), and parahippocampal gyrus (MSBB-BM36). The gene read counts were generated through a consensus bioinformatics pipeline that aligned raw RNA-Seq data files, counted reads mapped to genes, and reported quality control measures.

Further details can be found on the AD knowledge portal (https://adknowledgeportal.synapse.org, Synapse ID: syn17010685) and by Wan et al. The consensus bioinformatics pipeline details and quality control measures for the three RNA-Seq cohorts are documented under this Synapse ID.
Ensemble database queries used to examine gene names from RNA-Seq files relied upon http://dec2015.archive.ensembl.org/index.html for gene annotation and identification purposes.

For contemporary literature-based gene set derived from Neuner et al., http://aug2020.archive.ensembl.org/index.html was used. This archive was used to identify 112 genetic loci associated with AD and to perform post-hoc comparison of genes in the RNA-Seq dataset.

Brain tissue samples were obtained from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) NeuroBioBank with the MTA number NBB1001 and 1019. PLD1-associated protein complexes were isolated from crude synaptoneurosomal fractions (BA38) of FTD and control brains using antibody-based immunoprecipitation.

Brain tissue samples were obtained from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) NeuroBioBank with the MTA number NBB1001 and 1019. PLD1-associated protein complexes were isolated from crude synaptoneurosomal fractions (BA38) of FTD and control brains using antibody-based immunoprecipitation.

All data generated or analyzed during this study are included in this published article and its supplementary information files. Proteomic profiling of PLD1-associated complexes revealed compartment-specific alterations with cytosolic fractions enriched for metabolic enzymes, stress-response proteins, and GFAP. Peptides were prepared using S-Trap digestion, analyzed on an Orbitrap Fusion mass spectrometer coupled to nanoLC, and searched against the human proteome using Proteome Discoverer with Sequest. Label-free quantification was performed without imputation.

All summary statistics generated in this study are publicly available at 10.17863/CAM.128272. These include summary statistics for the 276 network edges and 2 genetic gradients for both MIND and FC phenotypes.

dataset_identifier: PGC-SCZ, PGC-MDD, PGC-ADHD, PGC-ASD, PGC-BPD, PGC-ALZ
dataset_context_from_paper: Summary statistics for schizophrenia (SCZ), major depressive disorder (MDD), attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), bipolar disorder (BPD), and Alzheimer's disease (ALZ) can be downloaded from https://pgc.unc.edu/for-researchers/download-results/
Summary statistics for C-reactive protein concentration (CRP) can be downloaded from https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gwas/summary_statistics/GCST90029001-GCST90030000/GCST90029070/

Summary statistics for Body Mass Index (BMI) can be downloaded from https://portals.broadinstitute.org/collaboration/giant/index.php/GIANT_consortium_data_files#2018_GIANT_and_UK_BioBank_Meta-analysis
Summary statistics for gestational duration (GEST) can be downloaded from https://egg-consortium.org/gestational-duration-2019.html
Code to calculate MIND networks can be accessed at 10.5281/zenodo.7974716.

This research has been conducted using the UK Biobank Resource under application number 20904. MRI data for MIND network construction was available for 21,447 UKB participants in 2024, with a maximum of 18,769 participants available for the replication GWAS. The discovery sample consisted of N max=30,524 individuals from the UKB.

All postmortem human data can be accessed through the Synapse AD Knowledge Portal (syn53461705), which also includes associated ROSMAP metadata. These data are subject to controlled access in compliance with human privacy regulations. To obtain the data, a data use agreement (DUA) must be completed. This requirement ensures the anonymity of ROSMAP study participants. The postmortem human PFC samples were used for transcriptional analysis of ABCA7 LoF gene changes across major cell types, with analysis identifying biological pathways correlated with ABCA7 LoF including pathways related to cellular stress and apoptosis, synaptic function, DNA repair, and metabolism.

All code used in this study is available on GitHub (https://github.com/djunamay/ABCA7lof2). All iPSC-related data are accessible through links provided in our code repositories. For a complete list of data availability and download links, please refer to the code repositories listed below.

The genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for the GM were obtained from the European Bioinformatics Institute's GWAS database. This database provides detailed records of the characteristics of various GM taxa. A total of 473 taxa were meticulously selected for analysis in this study, covering 10 phyla, 18 classes, 24 orders, 58 families, 143 genera, 213 species, and 7 unclassified microbial groups. These SNPs associated with gut microbiota were obtained from publicly available GWAS and used in the 2-sample Mendelian randomization analysis to investigate genetic causality between GM and CSF metabolites and Alzheimer's disease.

Data from the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study (MOST) is publicly available at the National Institute on Aging, Aging Research Biobank. The study includes clinical, demographic, radiographic data, and gait characteristics from participants followed over time. Authors used MOST data to develop a machine learning model using super-learning ensemble techniques to predict worsening knee pain and worsening physical function, achieving AUCs of approximately 0.60. The dataset includes baseline WOMAC scores, radiographic information, depressive symptoms, and gait measurements. Research data and image sets are de-identified in accordance with regulation 45 CFR 164.514(e). Study participants were recruited under local institutional review board approval through collaborating institutions at Boston University, University of Iowa, University of Alabama at Birmingham, and University of California at San Francisco.

Cohort includes 410 Controls, 100 MCI, and 249 AD cases with research consensus diagnoses, 38.4% self-identified African American (AA) individuals, with a subset of 478 cases with CSF AD biomarkers. Baseline plasma samples were analyzed for accuracy in classifying diagnosis and predicting progression (i.e., Control to MCI or MCI to AD). Paired samples for 244 participants were used to determine longitudinal changes. Plasma pTau217 levels were analyzed using AlzPath antibody and the Simoa HD platform. Median pTau217 levels were 0.318 pg/ml in Controls, 0.678 pg/ml in MCI, and 1.151 pg/ml in AD.

Transcriptomic and lipidomic data from the Religious Order Study-Memory Aging Project (ROS-MAP) were integrated to identify dysregulated lipids in the Lands Cycle pathway associated with cognitive decline independently of amyloid and tau pathologies. Lipidomic data was generated using the Biocrates AbsoluteIDQ p180 platform, a multiplexed targeted metabolomic assay covering lipids and metabolites including acylcarnitines, glycerophospholipids and sphingolipids. Coordinate changes in lipids were found dysregulated in association with both mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and the ApoEe4 genotype. WGCNA analysis identified dysregulated lipids within a single module which are substrates and products in the Lands Cycle for acyl chain remodeling.

data_repository: Available on reasonable request from the ALFA Study Investigators
dataset_context_from_paper: Data that support the findings of this study are available on reasonable request from the ALFA Study Investigators. The dataset includes demographics (age, education, sex), cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers (Aβ 42/40 ratio, p-tau, NFL, GFAP, sTREM2, SNAP-25, SYT1, S100b, YKL40), and clinical variables. Participants were clustered based on their CSF biomarker expression using unsupervised bottom-up agglomerative hierarchical clustering analysis with complete linkage and Euclidean distance. Raw biomarker distributions were z-score normalized across features and observations.

Whole-genome sequencing data for the Harmonized Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India (LASI-DAD) is available from the National Institute on Aging Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), accession number: NG00067–ADSP Umbrella. The dataset was used for gene set enrichment analysis of identified enriched variants located within gene bodies, with variants defined as located within a gene body if within the boundaries of the gene's transcription start and stop positions in GENCODE or with most severe functional consequence in VEP not intergenic.

Phenotype data are available at the Gateway to Global Aging website, https://g2aging.org/. These phenotype data accompany the whole-genome sequencing data from the Harmonized Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India (LASI-DAD) and include cognitive measures and clinical assessments such as the Hindi Mental State Examination (HMSE).

The GWAS Catalog (All Associations, v1.0.2; accessed April 22, 2024), a public database documenting published variant–trait associations, was queried to better characterize previous associations with identified variants.

data_repository: Available from lead contact upon reasonable request
dataset_context_from_paper: The CosMx raw data (metadata and associated count matrices) in this paper are available from the lead contact upon reasonable request. The dataset includes spatial transcriptomics data from mouse brain tissue analyzed using a 950 plex RNA panel. Single-cell expression profiles were constructed by tallying transcripts of each gene within designated cell areas. Data normalization was performed by dividing each cell's raw counts vector by its total counts. The dataset was processed through de novo cell clustering using PCA, Nearest Neighbor Network Construction, and Leiden Clustering via the Giotto package, resulting in identification of 10 major cell types including neurons, oligodendrocytes, pericytes, microglia, and astrocytes.

dataset_identifier: Reference gene expression profiles for cell type classification
data_repository: Based on comprehensive cell typing census of mouse brain by single-cell RNA sequencing
dataset_context_from_paper: Reference gene expression profiles used in supervised cell type classification. This reference profile was based on a comprehensive cell typing census of mouse brain by single-cell RNA sequencing. Based on the original reference profiles, 43 cell typing assignments were generated, which were further collapsed into 10 major cell types. Cell types were annotated based on specific gene markers including Gad2 and Slc32a1 for neurons, Mog for oligodendrocytes, Vtn for pericytes, Csf1r for microglia, and Gja1 for astrocytes.

Metabolomics data used in this study to develop a metabolic risk score (metRS) for assessing exposure to traffic-related air pollution (TRAP). The authors state: 'By using both simulated and real-world metabolomics data, this study provides a better understanding of the strengths and limitations of three variations of risk score approaches.' The metabolomics data was analyzed using mummichog (version 2.3) for pathway analysis, with mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) and retention time of selected metabolites processed through the tool. Only pathways with >20% coverage were included in final results.

The National Institutes of Health (NIH)-funded NeuroBioBank (NBB) was established in September 2013 as a national resource for investigators utilizing post-mortem human brain tissue and related biospecimens for their research to understand conditions of the nervous system such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and many others. The NBB operates through several biorepositories across the USA, each maintaining collections of human post-mortem brain tissue and related biospecimens. The NBB catalog comprises medical records, interview results, and neuropathological reports, and has information on clinical diagnosis, medical history, as well as results of whole-genome sequencing. The present study serves as a pilot effort, focusing on donors with PD, which represents less than 5% of the total number of pathology reports in the NBB.

Data dictionary developed in this study was built using the controlled access datasets distributed from the Department of Defense (DOD)- and National Institutes of Health (NIH)-supported Federal Interagency Traumatic Brain Injury Research (FITBIR) Informatics Systems. FITBIR is a collaborative biomedical informatics system created by the DOD and the NIH to provide a national resource to support and accelerate research in Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI).

Full expression, splicing and protein abundance xQTL summary statistics for 17 brain xQTL molecular contexts. The complete xQTL summary statistics will be available at the time of publication via The National Institute on Aging Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS). Data includes gene expressions summed into pseudo bulk counts for each donor-cell pair, quantified as counts per million (CPM) and quantile normalized from snRNA-seq data. SRM proteomics was performed on DLPFC with peptide relative abundances log2 transformed and centered at the median. All normalized molecular phenotypes were adjusted for technical factors (batch, RNA integrity number, post-mortem interval), biological covariates (sex, age at death), top 15 genotype PC, and hidden confounders using PCA.

Full colocalization results from xQTL-only and GWAS-xQTL ColocBoost analyses available through Synapse link for reviewers, with download information in Supplementary Table 1 including CoS and VCP scores. Second independent validation cohort of DLPFC samples from publicly available dataset used to test replicability of discovery cohort findings. Dataset contained 53 subclusters of interneurons. IN class proportions: SST 29.6%, PVALB 26.7%, CALB2/VIP 22.5%, LAMP5 12.8%, and CCK 8.5%. Hierarchical clustering comparing 37 IN subtypes from discovery cohort to 53 subclusters in validation cohort 2 showed 35 of 37 discovery cohort clusters were most similar to a cluster in validation cohort 2, including rare SST-36 subtype comprising 0.17% of IN population.

GTEx small RNA eQTL dataset used for analyzing microRNA expression quantitative trait loci. Authors used data from both RNA-seq (MIR containing host LINC genes, eQTL q < 0.1) and the small RNA-seq resource (GTEx small RNA eQTLs v10, eQTL q < 0.1). The dataset includes adult brain tissue small RNA expression data and was selected specifically for quantifying small RNA expression in brain tissues. All datasets reported only cis-eQTLs.

SFARI database used to identify autism spectrum disorder (ASD) risk genes. Authors examined differentially expressed genes to see if they were previously identified as risk genes for ASD using the SFARI database. Genes in the SFARI database with a high confidence score, strong candidate or syndromic classification were included in the analyses.

SysNDD is a curated database for genes identified in developmental delay, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder. Authors used this database to identify neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) risk genes among differentially expressed genes. Genes with limited or refuted evidence were excluded from the analyses. In total 2,526 ASD and NDD genes were included in the analyses.

Gene set enrichment analysis performed using GSEA with multiple gene set collections including KEGG_Legacy, KEGG_Medicus, Wikipathways, Reactome, GO Biological process, GO cellular component and GO molecular function to analyze gene set overlap of differentially expressed genes.
SynGO v1.2 database used to determine enrichment in synaptic cellular components and biological processes among differentially expressed genes.

Sequencing data is available from the authors on request. CLB designed the experiments and analyzed the RNA-sequencing data. YF performed the lab experiments. The authors generated RNA-sequencing data that was analyzed for differential gene expression.

Raw mass spectrometry data of all immunoprecipitation (IP) experiments have been deposited to the ProteomeXchange Consortium via the PRIDE partner repository with the dataset identifier PXD075357. The data were acquired using a Data-Independent-Acquisition (DIA) mode on a Bruker timsTOF HT mass spectrometer with a customized DIA-LFQ workflow. Raw data were processed using DIA-NN (version 1.8.1) with a reviewed UniProt human protein sequence database (Swiss-Prot, November 2023 release). Protein enrichment was assessed relative to GFP control using four biological replicates, with fold change calculated as the median of all possible ratios and statistical significance evaluated using an empirical Bayes framework implemented in the limma package.

A reviewed UniProt human protein sequence database (Swiss-Prot, November 2023 release; taxonomy ID 9606) was used for all DIA-NN searches to process raw mass spectrometry data acquired in data-independent acquisition mode.

scRNA-seq files for the BCBM analysis in Figure 8 are available through GEO SuperSeries accession number GSE147949. Samples were integrated using the IntegrateLayers command and the RPCAIntegration method followed by clustering using FindNeighbors, FindClusters, and RunUMAP commands.

Fine mapping GWAS risk loci for schizophrenia, depression and AD. Dataset used for linking SNPs within 99% credible sets to putative causal genes and assigning them based on transcript promoter overlap with fine-mapped risk variants and cell-type specific chromatin loops.

dataset_identifier: Single-nucleus transcriptomes across six human cortical areas
dataset_context_from_paper: Single-nucleus transcriptomes dataset across six human cortical areas with associated cell type annotations downloaded from the ALLEN BRAIN data portal. Used to generate pseudo-bulk data for each cell type to obtain gene expression levels in specific brain cell types. Gene expression levels determined by aggregating total reads assigned to genes across all cells in pseudo-bulk samples, normalized to one million reads followed by log2 transformation.

Pre-training dataset for INTERACT comprises approximately 25 million CpG sites obtained from pseudo-bulk tissue derived from 4,137 nuclei. DNAm levels determined by calculating ratio of methylated reads to total reads across all nuclei. Only CpG sites covered by more than 50 reads included for high data quality. Hi-C contact data collected for three broad cell types (neuron, ODC and astrocytes) from same prior study. Cell-type specific chromatin loops called from same nuclei at 10-kb resolution using SnapHiC method. Fine-tuning datasets for each cell type contained between 2.3 and 3.1 million CpG sites that were either fully methylated or fully unmethylated.

GENCODE version 42 basic gene annotations used to define promoters as 1-kb upstream and 1-kb downstream of transcript start site for assigning SNPs within 99% credible sets to putative causal genes based on transcript promoter overlap with fine-mapped risk variants.

The NACC database is funded by NIA/NIH Grant U24 AG072122. The paper references NACC as part of the AD cohort studies landscape that was harmonized using the AD-Mapper tool for semantic data harmonization of Alzheimer's disease cohort studies.

Nested case-control study of 375 randomly selected Generation Scotland participants with a first incident ischaemic stroke (IS), matched 1:1 to controls by age and sex. IFN-α levels were measured by ultra-sensitive digital ELISA on a fully automated Simoa HD-X platform using serum collected a median of 8.4 years before IS. Final analysis included 353 case-control pairs (n=706) with reliable IFN-α measurements (mean age=62.0 years [SD=11.8], 50.4% males). The median serum IFN-α concentration was 32.3 fg/mL (Q1-Q3: 21.3-53.5; range: 9.2-8,089.2 fg/mL). Associations between log-transformed IFN-α concentrations and IS risk were examined using conditional logistic regressions.

LIFE Study datasets are available through the NIA Aging Research Biobank. Study of older adults at high risk of mobility disability examining associations between plasma concentrations of 27 SASP (Senescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype) proteins and cognitive outcomes including mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia. The plasma concentrations of these 27 proteins were previously identified as components of the SASP that were elicited by several human senescent cell types and associated with chronological age and multimorbidity. Biomarker data presented in the current study will be made available by the investigative team upon reasonable request.

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01072500. Study of older adults at high risk of mobility disability examining associations between biomarkers (MPO, MMP, MMP1) and cognitive impairment outcomes including MCI and dementia.

Microarray dataset imported and processed using R packages GEOquery, Rcpp v1.0.12, and tidyselect v1.2.1. Datasets were created as subsets by diagnosis and sample type or brain region. Platform-specific IDs were converted into Entrez Gene IDs using Bioconductor annotation databases via bioMart v3.8. Multiple platform IDs matching the same gene were summarized with gene expression as the mean of probe expression. Differential expression analysis was performed with limma v3.8 with FDR-adjusted p value <0.1 as cut-off for differential expression. GSEA was performed on all genes ranked by log2FC using fgsea R package v1.31.0.

Public transcriptomic dataset sourced from GEO platform hosted on NCBI. Includes data from 1,053 postmortem brain samples across 19 brain regions from 125 patients dying at different AD stages, with 50-60 subjects per brain region. Patients were clustered by AD severity into four groups: normal (n=110), posAD (n=110), proAD (n=83) and defAD (n=163) groups, according to clinical dementia rating (CDR), Braak NFT score, sum of NFT density across brain regions, average neuritic plaque density and average CERAD score. Used for transcriptome meta-analysis.

Data presented in the manuscript and supplementary file are available to readers. Targeted proteomics analysis of microvessel samples measuring transporter abundances including ABCB1, ABCG2, Na+/K+-ATPase, GLUT1, GLUT3, LAT1, SLC1A2/EAAT2, SLC1A3/EAAT1, SLC29A1/ENT1, and SLC38A3/SNAT3. Immunoblotting of leftover microvessel samples confirmed presence of these transporters. Transporter abundances represent the average expression across 2-3 tumors pooled into each sample, with details of pooled specimens provided in Table S3.

NeuroBioBank, NIH, provided AD patient samples used in this study. Dorsal hippocampal subregion CA1 brain tissue was homogenized and analyzed for tau expression levels using real-time PCR. The tissue samples were processed to extract soluble tau fractions for Western blot analysis comparing PBS control, mQβ/tau admixture, and mQβ-tau vaccine groups.

Raw mouse sequencing data (hashtag reads) available from the Sequence Read Archive. Used for sample demultiplexing in single-nucleus RNA sequencing experiments with hashtag labeling.
Processed and raw mouse expression data available from the Single Cell Portal. Contains single-nucleus RNA-seq profiles from mouse cortex samples. Source data underlying Fig. 2b.

RNA-seq dataset from Parkinson's disease (PD) patients and healthy control samples. Gene counts were normalized using edgeR (TMM) and tested for significant differential expression with Limma and Voom. Differential gene expression analysis compared all PD samples vs. healthy control samples, with volcano plots showing genes annotated with biological process GO category 'protein folding' and the eight primary subunits of the CCT complex. Additional analysis compared asymmetry (severe vs. moderate hemisphere) across all PD samples. Gene set enrichment analysis was performed using GSEA and STRING V.12.

Longitudinal MRI scans from LBC1936 cohort used for genome-wide investigations of brain atrophy (LBA). MRI acquisition and initial analyses were conducted at the Brain Research Imaging Centre, Neuroimaging Sciences, University of Edinburgh. The study included meticulously collected longitudinal MRI scans and performed GWAS in participants from this cohort. LBA was substantially heritable (h2 SNP GCTA = 41% [95% CI = 38–43%]).

All UKB data analysed here were provided under project reference 10279. UKB participants attended one of four testing sites (Cheadle ~60%, Reading ~14%, Newcastle ~25%, Bristol ~0.13%). The same type of scanner was used in all four testing sites, a 3T Siemens Skyra with a 32-channel Siemens head radiofrequency coil. T1-weighted MPRAGE volumes were exclusively used with 208 sagittal slices acquired with field view of 256 mm and matrix size of 256 × 256 pixels, giving resolution of 1 × 1 × 1 mm³. Regional data were extracted from bulk-downloaded aseg files provided by UK Biobank using FreeSurfer v6.0. Values more than 4 standard deviations from the mean for any global or subcortical brain structure volume were excluded (corresponding to <1.2% of data per variable).

GenScot study data were accessed for analysis. MRI protocols for GenScot are reported elsewhere but briefly summarised. GenScot parcellations have previously undergone quality control with manual editing to rectify parcellation issues including skull stripping, tissue identification and regional boundary lines. Original pipeline used for small RNA-seq analysis is available on github. The pipeline was used for processing and analyzing small RNA sequencing datasets, including tRNA fragment classification following the tRAX framework and differential expression analysis using DESeq2.

RNA-seq dataset generated from muscle fibers (MFs) and satellite fibers (SFs). FastQ files were generated via Illumina bcl2fastq2 from raw sequencing reads produced by Illumina NextSeq sequencer. Gene and transcript intensities were computed using STAR/RSEM software using GRCh38 (Gencode Release 27) as reference. Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2 with |log2(MFs/SFs)| ≥1 and FDR ≤0.1 thresholds. Deregulated genes were subjected to pathway analysis using KEGG, WikiPathways, and gene ontology enrichment via enrichR. Technical validation was conducted using qPCR. The dataset includes differentially expressed coding and non-coding genes with pathway enrichment results showing 29 deregulated pathways including ECM-receptor interaction pathway with 11 coding genes.

The study used dementia cohort identification to select cases and controls from EMR datasets using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes for different dementia types.

All available MRI brain scans collected as part of routine NHS medical practice for Tayside and Fife participants in these studies were obtained from the SMI. SHARE is supported by NHS Research Scotland, Universities in Scotland and the Chief Scientists Office. Recruitment to this study was facilitated by SHARE. All files, including the scripts used for Seurat gene expression analyses are available on Dryad. Cell clusters were identified and cell types were assigned based on expression of pre-defined marker genes. The data includes analysis of astrocyte classes showing expression of Aldh1l1, S100β, GLT, Kir4.1, GAT-3, LRRK2, and PPM1H genes.

dataset_context_from_paper: Single-cell RNA-seq dataset from endothelial cells (ECs) with multiple subtypes (Cap EC1, Cap EC2, Art EC, Ven EC1, Ven EC2). Differential expression analysis was performed using DESeq2 on pseudobulk profiles aggregated per biological replicate. DEGs were defined as those with adjusted p < 0.05 and |log₂FC| ≥ 1. The dataset was analyzed for metabolic states across EC subtypes using SPECTRA package, with focus on biotin metabolism genes (Slc16a1, Btd, Slc5a6, Slc19a3) and subtype-specific markers (Mfsd2a for Cap EC1, Bmx for Art EC, Nr2f2 for Ven EC1, Vcam1 for Ven EC2, Plvap for Cap EC2). Pathway enrichment analysis was performed using Enrichr and Metascape, with protein-protein interaction analysis using String (v12.0).

All brain samples were obtained from the Mayo Clinic Brain Bank, which operates under the approval of the Mayo Clinic Institutional Review Board. The optimized CLEM protocol has been successfully applied to the identification and analysis of proteinaceous inclusions in both cell model and postmortem human brain tissue.

Comprehensive whole genome sequence analysis identifying SNVs, indels and SVs contributing to the risk of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP). The study replicated previously reported risk regions in MAPT, MOBP, STX6, SLCO1A2, DUSP10, and SP1, and discovered novel loci in APOE, FCHO1/MAP1S, KIF13A, TRIM24, ELOVL1, and TNXB. Heritability of PSP for common SNVs and indels (MAF > 0.01) was estimated at 20%, while common plus rare SNVs/indels was estimated at 23%. Rare variant aggregated tests identified ZNF592 with significant association (SKAT-O FDR=0.043, burden test FDR=0.041). Samples were provided by Biobanc-Hospital Clinic-FRCB-IDIBAPS and Center for Neurodegenerative Disease Research at Penn.

Analysis pipeline and code repository for whole genome sequencing analysis of PSP. Contains methods for SNV, indel and SV calling using Manta (v1.6.0), Smoove (v0.2.5), Svimmer, and Graphtyper2 (v2.7.3) for joint genotyping. Includes quality filtering procedures using Samplot and IGV for CNVs, inversions, and insertions, and heritability estimation using GCTA-LDMS.

dataset_context_from_paper: This study is a subset of 2769 suicide deaths from the USMRS sample with electronic health records, clinical notes for natural language processing (NLP), and genome-wide genotyping data. This subset represents 17.59% of the deaths in the study collection period, from December 1998 through October 2022. Whole blood was collected from persons who died by suicide when suicide determination was made by the Utah State Office of the Medical Examiner following detailed investigation. When sufficient sample amounts were available, high-quality DNA was extracted. Identifiers from suicide deaths were securely transferred to staff at the Utah Population Database, a state-wide database of more than 11 million individuals. The staff linked health records and supplied clinical notes to a suicidality-detecting NLP algorithm.
